primitives.verbatim_quote: The raw ECG signal was first bandpass filtered (0.5 - 35 Hz) to attenuate baseline wander and high-frequency noise.
primitives.latex: X(f) = \mathcal{F}\{x(t)\} \cdot H(f), \quad H(f) = \begin{cases} 1, & f_{low} \leq f \leq f_{high} \\ 0, & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: x(t): Raw electrocardiographic voltage (mV); X(f): Frequency domain representation (mV/Hz); H(f): Dimensionless filter transfer function; f: Frequency (Hz); f_low: Lower cutoff frequency (0.5 Hz); f_high: Upper cutoff frequency (35 Hz).
primitives.assumptions: Linearity and time-invariance of the filtering process; additive nature of baseline wander and high-frequency sensor noise relative to the underlying cardiac depolarization signal.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Signal-to-noise ratio drops below unity, or extreme motion artifacts induce non-stationary frequency shifts that alias directly into the 0.5-35 Hz passband, rendering R-peak detection mathematically unstable.

primitives.name: Autonomic Spectral Decomposition
primitives.verbatim_quote: From the artifact-corrected RR interval series, standard frequencydomain HRV parameters were computed using Kubios., The extracted indices included: very low frequency (VLF: 0.01 - 0.04 Hz), low frequency (LF: 0.04 - 0.15 Hz), high frequency (HF: 0.15 - 0.40 Hz), the LF/HF ratio, and total power.
primitives.latex: P(f) = \left| \frac{1}{\sqrt{N}} \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} x[n] e^{-j 2 \pi f n} \right|^2, \quad \text{Ratio}_{LF/HF} = \frac{\int_{0.04}^{0.15} P(f) df}{\int_{0.15}^{0.40} P(f) df}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: P(f): Power spectral density (ms^2/Hz); x[n]: Equidistantly resampled RR interval time series (ms); N: Number of samples; Ratio_LF/HF: Sympathovagal balance index (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: The RR interval series can be accurately equidistantly resampled without introducing significant interpolation bias; autonomic control mechanisms manifest as linear superpositions of distinct oscillatory processes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Severe non-stationarity caused by abrupt physical exertion or massive sympathetic surges, violating the Fourier assumption of cyclostationarity within the analysis window.
